resources.string: Every floor is a room of your real home, and every chore is a spell. The tower looks the way your home is kept.
Each spell has its own rhythm: dishes daily, linen every two weeks. As the days pass it fades and the floor gathers dust. Nothing burns and there are no streaks to lose.
When a spell is past due, a little imp moves onto its floor. They\'re harmless, they only giggle. Doing the chore chases them off.
Tap a floor, then the tick next to a spell once you\'ve done the chore for real. You get mana, and your helpers wake as you master spells. Tapped by mistake? Undo is right there.
Each week I ask for three spells: they pay double mana. On a tired day, \"Low on energy\" shows only small spells. And I\'ll write to you every week.
Its spells, most urgent first. The bar shows how fresh each one is: green is bright, orange is fading, purple means imps.
The big tick casts a spell, the pencil edits it. Hold a spell to open its page in the grimoire. Up top you can furnish the floor or change it.
Only the quick chores, a few minutes each, most urgent first. Even a small spell drives the imps out.
Every spell you cast takes you closer to the next circle of apprenticeship. Mana is what you spend in the decor shop.
Each helper looks after a few spells. Cast them five times and it wakes up and moves into the tower; at 20, 50 and 100 casts it grows a level.
A spell grows from Novice to Apprentice, Adept, Master and Archmage as you cast it. The calendar shows the last twelve weeks.
Its level, the spells that feed it and the floor it calls home. Keep casting those spells and it grows.
Your shopping list. Type what you need: the stall is guessed for you, and you can tap it to change.
I remember how often you buy things and suggest them when they\'re probably running out. When you head out, open the market trip.
Tick things as they go in the basket. When you\'re done, the trip counts as the market spell, if your tower has one.
I write once a week from my travels. The newest letter carries this week\'s three requests.
Spend mana on things for the tower. A floor holds four; the rest wait in the chest until you place them.
Set how often the chore needs doing and how big it is: small spells give 5 mana, usual ones 10, great ones 20. Pick the helper it feeds.
Order the floors the way you like, top to bottom, or add a new room.
